lesson: In downtime_minutes, merge both overlapping and touching incident windows where an alert starts exactly when another ends before summing minutes.
why: Summing alerts independently double- or triple-counts minutes during concurrent alerts for the same outage.
quote: make sure touching windows merge too - an alert that starts exactly when another ends is the same outage, counted once.

lesson: In the report job, log at DEBUG level using only one summary line per tenant per run with the merged window count, rejecting per-decision logging.
why: The job iterates over every tenant nightly and previously exceeded log quotas when logging excessively.
quote: Debug level, and one summary line per tenant per run with the merged window count - not per decision

lesson: In downtime_minutes, apply the 60-second blip exclusion to merged outage windows instead of dropping raw pre-merge incidents, counting outages of 60 seconds or greater in full.
why: Dropping pre-merge incidents misclassifies real chained outages, such as two 40-second alerts forming an 80-second outage.
quote: The threshold applies AFTER merging, to the merged window: if the merged outage is under 60 seconds it's a monitoring blip

lesson: In downtime_minutes, evaluate whether a merged window is a blip before performing any maintenance subtraction.
why: A merged outage exceeding the threshold is a legitimate outage even if scheduled maintenance later accounts for most of its duration.
quote: Blip check first, on the merged window as measured - a 90-second merged outage is not a blip

lesson: In downtime_minutes, subtract maintenance only if announced_at is at least 24 hours prior to the window start, subtracting solely the intersection clamped at zero and rejecting blanket maintenance subtraction.
why: Under SLA addendum terms, short-notice maintenance cannot penalize customer uptime credits, and all maintenance records reliably contain announced_at.
quote: Maintenance reduces downtime only when it was properly announced: at least 24 hours between announced_at and the window start

lesson: In downtime_minutes, return fractional downtime minutes untouched as a float, rejecting any rounding to whole numbers.
why: Downstream billing handles rounding when issuing credit memos, and applying multiple layers of rounding causes calculation discrepancies.
quote: Keep fractional - billing does the rounding downstream at credit-memo time, and two layers of rounding is how the last dispute started.
